newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan president denies Iranian interference.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan president denies Iranian interference.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari on Wednesday denied a charge by a militant Sunni Moslem group that Iran was interfering in Pakistan's internal affairs.
"We have brotherly relations with Iran and consider them as our brothers," he told a news conference during a visit to Quetta, capital of the province of Baluchistan bordering Iran and Afghanistan.

The Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group accused Tehran of interference and blamed a Shi'ite Moslem group for a weekend bomb blast in Lahore, capital of Punjab province, which killed SSP leader Zia-ur-Rahman Faruqi and 26 other people.
Leghari denied a reporter's suggestion that Iran, Saudi Arabia, Iraq and other Moslem countries were involved in whipping up tension between rival Moslem groups in Pakistan.
"They are not interfering in our internal affairs," he said.

Leghari said he regretted that SSP activists sacked and burned the Iranian cultural centre in Lahore, drawing a protest from Tehran. "We will give adequate protection to all Iranians in Pakistan," he said.
Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's 130 million people. They are a majority in Iran.

Police said on Monday a Shi'ite activist named Mehram Ali had confessed to detonating the bomb by remote control as Faruqi and his deputy, Azam Tariq, arrived at a Lahore court on Saturday to face charges of being involved in the murders of several Shi'ites.
